why: Entry already right for the only line, a13.p7 ਸੰਤ ਕੈ ਦੋਖਿ ਨ ਤ੍ਰਿਸਟੈ ਕੋਇ: 'is satisfied' (तृप्त होता है) agrees with our Hindi, our new English and the standard translations, and fits a derivation from Skt tuṣṭa (satisfied). The writer's 'stands firm' (from tiṣṭhati) was offered only as 'possibly' (doubts a13.p7), and I could not confirm it in any reference available here (Mahan Kosh, Sahib Singh), so it is not added. Worth checking later against those.
